case_name: Anju Thakur vs Ut Of Jammu & Kashmir

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Anju Thakur, wife; Ashok Singh, husband; Oma Devi, mother; Ambica Kumar, sister; Neeraj Singh, brother

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife alleged cruelty by her husband and in-laws. She registered an FIR and a criminal case was initiated. A reconciliation exercise led to a compromise between the parties.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise agreement can be a valid basis for quashing criminal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: The petitioners have come forward with the present petition invoking inherent jurisdiction of this Court under section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 seeking quashment of a criminal case born out of FIR No. 0383 dated 29.12.2020 read with Final Police Report No. 107/2021 dated 21.06.2021.

legal_principles.principle: A party's willingness to withdraw accusations and allegations can be a factor in quashing criminal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner No. 1 has also agreed for withdrawing of her accusations and allegations against the petitioners No. 2 to 5 and also for withdrawal of her domestic violence case as well as maintenance case against the petitioners No. 2 to 5.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
